newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Zastava workers protests enter 5th week.
newsitem.headline: Zastava workers protests enter 5th week.

text.p: Workers in Yugoslavia's biggest arms manufacturer Zastava entered the fifth week of their protest over unpaid wages on Monday and said they wanted the group's general manager sacked.

"We are getting ready together with the car plant's union to demand the dismissal of Zastava group general manager," union president Zoran Nedeljkovic told Reuters by telephone from the factory in Kragujevac south of Belgrade.
"Workers from Zastava car manufacturer joined us today and we expect more people from other factories to join us tomorrow," he said.

Zastava workers have staged protests in the town's main square during working hours for the past four weeks demanding unpaid wages, holiday pay for the past two years, and a programme to revive production.
"This year's holiday pay is a condition for our talks with the management," Nedeljkovic said.
Nedeljkovic rejected accusations by local authorities that the protests were turning into political meetings.
He did not give any figure on the number of people at Monday's protest but said the turnout was the biggest since the protest began.
"We will continue to protest until all our demands are met," Nedeljkovic said.
